overview_html: In this live cohort Socratic session for Lesson 7.1: Boolean Logic 101: True/False Legal Gates, participants examine how static paper contracts transform into active software runtimes through a 3-step Boolean translation bridge (isolating the legal obligation, defining a binary true/false primitive, and embedding it in an if/else gate), why natural-language "and/or" vagueness crashes deterministic runtimes without strict data typing domains, how John Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory, Jerome Bruner's Spiral Curriculum, and Siegfried Engelmann's Direct Instruction govern the /101/idea/ 3-Tier Depth & Breadth Map, how REPSL osFig (🔱) Confidential VMs (repsl-lex) and US Patent 12,664,142 (SeedTree) reduce platform engineering costs by 70%, and how the DAO Coalition shields decentralized communities (such as Artizen DAO) from CFTC v. Ooki DAO general-partnership liability using Wyoming DUNA (Wyo. Stat. § 17-32-101 et seq.) wrappers and Decile Hub PACT commitments.

takeaways.body_html: Decoupling passive data from active instructions by isolating legal obligations, defining binary true/false primitives (== vs. right-to-left = assignment), Eliminating the "and/or" ambiguity trap via data typing domains, and chaining Hats Protocol role trees.

Operating stateful agent VMs (repsl-lex) inside the osFig (🔱) enclave over persistent GNU screen PTY multiplexers (2 GB save states, $3/mo static IPs) while US Patent 12,664,142 prevents DOM/localStorage collisions and cuts build costs by 70%.
